July 25, 2020
Angela Mahoney
General Manager
Johnson, Cross and Gibbs
Dear Ms. Mahoney,
This letter sets out the terms on which we will carry out a service line assessment
for Johnson, Cross and Gibbs, and I am glad to be putting them in writing, because a
shared understanding of the work is worth as much at the outset as any finding we
will hand you at the end. What follows describes the scope we have agreed, the
people who will do the work, the fee and when it begins, and the standard terms we
both sign up to. If any part of it reads differently from the conversation we had,
please say so before you countersign, so that the document we both hold to is the
same one.
The work we have agreed
The assessment looks at your service lines and asks a plain question of each of
them, which is whether it earns its keep once its true costs are set honestly against
what it actually brings in. We will build that picture from your own cost accounting
and volumes rather than from national benchmarks alone, because a line that looks
marginal against an outside figure often looks quite different once its local
economics are laid out in full. Where a line's performance turns on how physician
effort is compensated, or on where the revenue cycle is losing what the line has
already earned, we will follow the question into those areas rather than stop at the
edge of the ledger.
Our habit is to lead with what the numbers support and to label a recommendation
as a recommendation rather than dress it up as a finding, and you should expect
that discipline from us throughout. Nothing we put in front of you will assert a
conclusion the analysis has not earned, and where the evidence is genuinely mixed
we will tell you so plainly instead of resolving it for the sake of a cleaner page. That
is slower in a given week, and it is the only way we know to produce work that holds
up when someone outside the room reads it closely.
Verdant Health Advisory LLC
Page 1 of 4

Who will do the work
Daniel Alvarado, our Senior Consultant, will lead the assessment day to day and will
be your point of contact for anything of substance, and he is the person who will
reconcile your cost accounting until each line finally tells the truth. Susan Clark, a
Principal in our advisory practice, will take up any question that touches physician
compensation, and she is careful with fair-market-value language precisely because
she reaches for it only where the analysis has earned it. Patricia Moore, an Analyst
with us, will carry the revenue-cycle work, following a denied claim through every
handoff that touched it, and she is often the one who asks the question the rest of us
had assumed was already answered.
I will not run the work week to week, but I read everything before it reaches you,
and I am reachable directly if the assessment is not going the way you expected. If
that ever becomes your concern, I would ask you to call me rather than wait for the
next scheduled update.
Fee and when we begin
Our fee for the assessment is $53,000, fixed at the outset so that neither of us has to
reopen the commercial question once the work is under way. We expect the
assessment to run roughly seven months from commencement, and the work begins
on August 4, 2020. The terms below set out how that fee is billed and the small
number of protections we each carry.
Fees and payment
The fixed fee is billed in equal monthly installments across the term of the
assessment, the first on your countersignature and the commencement of the work
and the remainder on the same day of each month thereafter, without regard to the
particular stage the assessment has reached in any given month. Reasonable and
documented out-of-pocket costs, meaning travel to your sites and any external data
or verification you ask us to commission, are billed at cost as incurred and itemized
on each invoice. Invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt.
Term and termination
The engagement runs from the commencement date named above until we deliver
the completed assessment, and either of us may end it earlier on thirty days' written
notice. If you end it, you owe the installments that have fallen due as of that date
together with the costs incurred to that point, and nothing beyond them. If we end
it, which we would do only if the work as defined had become one we could not
complete honestly, we will return any amount paid for work not yet performed.
Verdant Health Advisory LLC
Page 2 of 4

Confidentiality
The information you will open to us, your cost accounting, your compensation
arrangements, and the operating detail beneath them, is confidential, and we will
use it only for this assessment and disclose it to no one outside the team named
above without your agreement. We ask the same of you for the analysis and working
materials we provide, which are yours to use inside your organization for the
decisions this work is meant to inform and are not for wider circulation. Because
some of what we examine touches physician compensation, we will handle that
material with the added care its sensitivity deserves.
Limitation of liability
We will carry out the assessment with the care and skill customary in our
profession, and we will tell you what the evidence supports, but the decisions that
follow from it are yours to make and we do not warrant their outcome. The analysis
rests on the completeness and accuracy of the data you provide us, and while we
will test what can reasonably be tested and flag what we cannot, we do not
independently audit your books. Our aggregate liability under this engagement, on
any theory, is limited to the fees actually paid to us for it, and neither of us is liable
to the other for indirect or consequential loss, save that nothing here limits liability
for our own fraud or willful misconduct.
Governing law
This letter is the whole of our agreement on this assessment and supersedes
anything said or drafted before it, and it is governed by the law of the state in which
our firm keeps its principal office, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Any
dispute we cannot settle between ourselves belongs to the courts sitting in that
state, and any change to these terms is effective only in writing signed by us both.
If this reflects our agreement
If this letter matches what we agreed, please countersign where indicated and
return a copy to me, and Daniel Alvarado will be in touch within the week to arrange
the intake session and the first data request. I would ask that you bring the people
who own the service-line and revenue-cycle numbers into that first session together,
because the work goes faster and lands better when everyone who holds a piece of
the picture hears the same questions at the same time.
We are glad you asked us to take this on, and we will give it the care it deserves.
With kind regards,
Verdant Health Advisory LLC
Page 3 of 4

Laura Brown
Managing Partner
Date: July 25, 2020
Angela Mahoney
General Manager, Johnson, Cross and Gibbs
Date: July 25, 2020
Verdant Health Advisory LLC
